title: Role swap preserves protocol output
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice's inputs drawn from $X$, Bob's inputs drawn from $Y$, and outputs in $\alpha$, and let $x : X$ and $y : Y$ be inputs. Then executing the role-swapped protocol on the input pair $(y, x)$ returns the same value as executing $p$ on $(x, y)$.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic protocol p over input types X (Alice) and Y (Bob) with outputs in α
an input x : X for Alice
an input y : Y for Bob
replaced:
For any protocol $p$ over $X \times Y$ and any inputs $x : X$, $y : Y$,
\[
  p.\texttt{swap}.\texttt{run}\;y\;x \;=\; p.\texttt{run}\;x\;y.
\]
